en: Homage to you, who have transcended the world and perceive the knowledge of solitude;
you who, out of compassion, have long been weary for the sake of the welfare of the world.
It is your view that there is no sentient being existing apart from the mere aggregates.
And for the sake of sentient beings, O Great Sage, you underwent supreme exhaustion.
Those very aggregates, O wise one, have been fully revealed by you to the wise as being like an illusion,
a mirage, a city of the Gandharvas, and a dream.

How indeed could those things which arise from causes and do not exist in their absence not be clearly considered equal to reflections? (NagLok 04) How can that which is visual be composed of the elements, which are themselves imperceptible to the eye?

By speaking thus regarding form, you have refuted the grasping of form. Since there is no sensation without that which is to be felt, sensation is therefore selfless; and it is your view that this object of feeling does not exist by way of its own intrinsic nature.
If name and object were non-different, the mouth would be burned by fire;

if they were different, there would be no comprehension—this was stated by you, the speaker of truth. You have also stated, according to conventional usage, that the agent is independent and so too is the action.
Yet you maintain that the establishment of these two is mutually dependent.
There is no agent and no enjoyer; merit and demerit are born dependently.
O Lord of Speech, you have declared that whatever is dependently arisen is not [inherently] born.
That which is not being known cannot be an object of knowledge, nor can there be consciousness without it;
therefore, you have stated that both knowledge and the object of knowledge do not exist by way of intrinsic nature.
If the characteristic were different from the characterized, then that characterized would be without a characteristic.

The non-existence of those two when they are not distinct has been clearly stated by you. This world, devoid of the characterized and the characteristic and free from the utterance of speech, was seen by you with the eye of wisdom as peaceful.
An entity that exists does not arise, nor does one that does not exist, nor one that both exists and does not exist.
It is not born from itself, nor from another, nor from both; how then could it be born?
For the destruction of an existing thing that is endowed with stability is not possible.
How could there be the cessation of a non-existent thing, which is equivalent to a horse’s horn?
It is held that the destruction of entities is neither different from them nor non-different from them;
if it were different, it would be eternal, and if it were not different, it would not exist [as a distinct event].
For if there is identity, the destruction of an entity is not tenable;
if there is difference, the destruction of an entity is not tenable.
First of all, the arising of an effect from a cause that has already perished is not logical.
Nor do you maintain that an arising equal to a dream occurs from what has not perished.
The sprout does not arise from a seed that has ceased, nor from one that has not ceased;
indeed, you state that all arising is like the arising of an illusion.
Therefore, you have thoroughly understood that this world arises from conceptual construction; it is unreal, unarisen, and does not perish.
There is no transmigration for the permanent, nor is there any transmigration for the impermanent.

"O best among those who know reality, you have declared that cyclic existence is like a dream. Logicians maintain that suffering is self-caused, caused by another, caused by both, or causeless; but you have stated that it arises dependently."
That which is dependent origination is itself considered by you to be emptiness;
"there is no independent entity"—this is your incomparable lion’s roar.
The teaching of the nectar of emptiness is for the destruction of all conceptual constructions.

Whosoever had a grasping even for that [emptiness], he has been subdued by you. O Protector, you have revealed that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature— inactive, powerless, empty, and arisen from conditions like an illusion.
Nothing has been produced by you, nor has anything been ceased;
as it was before, so it is after—you have awakened to suchness.
Indeed, without having relied upon this cultivation practiced by the Noble Ones, [you could not have done so].
For consciousness here cannot possibly be signless in any way whatsoever.
You have stated that there is no liberation without resorting to the signless;
therefore, you have taught that [signlessness] in its entirety within the Mahāyāna.
By whatever merit I have gained through praising you, the worthy object of praise,
who are free from the bonds of causal signs— by that may the entire world be liberated.
Thus ends the *Lokātīta-stava*.
